1425: the '14' is heavily inked/retouched but reads 14. 1440: third digit has an ink drop on it (reads 4), last digit an open-topped 0. Line ends with a dash carrying the word over to line 13. Pen lines beneath: a short line beneath the right part of 1425; a long line with hooked end beneath the latter half of 1440 and all of 1348. 10 groups.

Period after 1333 is a heavy blot. 512 written with 1 as a slanted stroke joined to the flag of the 5. Mark after 620 is a double cross (one bar with two short uprights, like ++ or #), followed by a period. Line ends with a dash carrying over to line 14. Pen lines beneath: thin short line beneath the first two digits of 1333; line beneath 1589 passing through the tail of its 9; line with hooked end beneath 1513. 11 groups.

1110: third digit overwritten/crossed (looks like an X), last digit a 0 with a rising top flick: alt 1140, 1116. Dash after 1110 sits low. 709: 0 has a looped top. Period after 788 uncertain (only a dot set high between 788 and 856). 856: last digit 6 with hooked ascender (0 much less likely). NO period or dash visible between 1517 and 1258 (long descender of the 7 and interlinear writing occupy the gap). 1258: small speck between 2 and 5; mark after it is a plain small +, then a period. Pen lines beneath: line beneath the second half of 1448 and 1018; long rising line beneath 1371. 171. running from the tail of the 9 of 709 to the tail of the 7 of 171; a thin line just under 856 that is probably the cross-stroke of interlinear writing below. 11 groups.

12?4: third digit under an ink smear/blot, unreadable (3, 5, 8, 2 or 1 possible). 51: first digit has a flag top and a curled foot (5) but interlinear strokes touch it: alt 91; the period after it is doubled (blot above a dot). 709 followed by two dots. 1244: second 4 is followed by a heavy hooked stroke that appears to be an ascender of interlinear writing below; NO period or dash visible after 1244. 13??: last two digits heavily overwritten/blotted solid; outline shows a round third digit and a final digit with a tall loop and long descending tail (9, less likely 7): candidates 1399, 1309, 1389, 1369; only '13' and the following dash are certain. Line ends with a dash carrying over to line 16. Pen line beneath 982-1104 (starts just left of the tail of the 9 of 982). 11 groups.

1110 followed by a small plain + and a period (a second stray dot above the period). 1348: second digit is a filled blob, 3 or 5: alt 1548. 770: a tick/dot before the first 7; period doubled. 1298: fourth digit heavily written and run into a blot from the interlinear layer; shows two counters like an 8 but could be 9 (alt 1299, less likely 1290); NO period visible after it (blot). Mark after 1258 is a double cross (bar with two wavy uprights, like the one after 620), then a period. 1362: the 3 and 6 are partly covered by an interlinear blot. 99: second 9 has a short stem; dash after it is wavy. Line ends with a dash carrying over to line 17. Pen line beneath 1228, ending in the tail of the 9 of 924. 11 groups.

350: the 5 is crowded by interlinear strokes. 1184: third digit blotted, shows a lower counter (8 or 6; 5 not excluded): alt 1164, 1154. 1176: the two 1s are joined at the foot by a blot (tip of an interlinear ascender?), so the pair could be read as an open-topped 4: alt 476. 146: last digit a ring with a short stub at top right: 6 preferred, alt 140; period doubled. 1362: a short black vertical tick crosses the base stroke of the 2 (possible mark beneath the group, or accidental). 99 followed by a period; beneath it a pen line running into a heavy blot (looks like a struck-out interlinear word over the next line). 1517: first 1 has a short cross-stroke near the top (contact with interlinear writing?); the separator after 1517 is a blobby dot with a short lead-in stroke: period preferred, alt dash (1517-1513). 1513 followed by two dots. Line ends with a dash carrying over to line 18. Pen line beneath the end of 1176 and 856. 12 groups.

1354: second digit small with curled foot, 3 or 5, crowded by the large flag of the following 5 (whose bowl is blotted closed): alt 1554. 1490 followed by two dots. 1112: foot of the second 1 touched by an interlinear ascender. 1392: the separator after it is an s-shaped squiggle joined to the base stroke of the 2 (taken as a period run into the 2; could conceivably be a letter s or a short dash); a pen line runs from the tail of the 9 rightward beneath '92'. 134 followed by two dots. 11 groups.

614: first digit is a ring with a short thick stub rising at upper right, where it runs into interlinear writing: 6 preferred, alt 814. 611: same form of first digit: 6 preferred, alt 811. 1465: 4 open-topped. A stray dot sits below the dash after 1563. 1300: final digit is a ring with a short flat bar at the top running right: 0 preferred, alt 1306. Code ends with 1547 and a period. 11 groups.
